Modern.tagline: Container freight in the trade's universal unit.
Modern.brandNameRationale: TEU — Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit, the universal capacity unit of container shipping, defined by the ISO 668 standard; every port, ship, and rate sheet in the world is denominated in TEU. Strongest of Agent A's three for modern: 'McLean Freight' is fine but reads as a generic surname (and slightly heritage); 'Ideal X Logistics' is specific but obscure. TEU is the actual trade-word every freight forwarder uses every day, instantly readable to anyone in shipping.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern container brokerage in 2025+ serves shippers who used to use a forwarder and now want a digital interface. Flexport, Forto, and Beacon set the template. The opening is for a brand that talks rate, TEU, and lane in plain language.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Flexport (flexport.com) holds the digital-forwarder peer position. Forto (forto.com) is the European equivalent. Beacon (beacon.io) sits in the visibility tier. Freightos (freightos.com) is the marketplace peer. We sit closer to Flexport, sharper on rate.
Modern.positioningStatement: A digital container broker named for the trade's universal unit.

targetAudience.primary: Operations and supply-chain leads at 50-2000 person product companies. Books 20-2000 TEU/year. Wants real-time rates, one named contact, and a portal that shows the box on a map.
behaviors: Books by lane, not by carrier
Will switch forwarders over a single missed cutoff

dos: Lead with rate, lane, and TEU
Publish the cutoff and the ETA
Sign quotes by the named broker

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only — TEU & Co in a tight modern grotesk, all caps. The negative space inside the U is a tiny container-shape rectangle. The U-as-container alone is the favicon.

colorPalette.name: Stack Orange
colorPalette.meaning: Single accent. The colour of a Hapag-Lloyd box.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for container numbers and rates
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the unit data; the regular carries the brand.

Luxury.tagline: White-glove freight in the merchant-league tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: The Hanseatic League — the medieval commercial confederation of north-German and Baltic merchant cities (Lübeck, Hamburg, Bremen, Bergen) that dominated European trade from the 12th to 17th centuries and codified maritime law. Strongest of Agent A's three for luxury: 'Lascaris & Co' is historically rich but obscure; 'Bill of Lading House' is too document-specific. Hanseatic is broadly recognisable, signals serious maritime heritage, and supports a premium white-glove positioning for fine-art and high-value freight.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury freight in 2025+ serves auction houses, fine-art dealers, fashion houses, and HNW individuals moving high-value goods. The category is dominated by Crozier, Atelier 4, and a few European specialists. The opening is for a brand with merchant-house heritage register.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Crozier Fine Arts (crozierfinearts.com) holds the fine-art-logistics peer. Atelier 4 (atelier4.com) sits at the same tier. Constantine Group (constantine.co.uk) is the UK heritage peer. Hasenkamp (hasenkamp.com) does the German equivalent. We sit smaller, more discreet.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A white-glove freight house in the Hanseatic merchant tradition.

targetAudience.primary: Auction-house operations directors, fashion-house logistics leads, private collectors with multi-residence shipping needs. They book by call, expect named handlers, and pay against itemised certificates.
behaviors: Schedules every consignment with a named handler
Expects continuity of relationship over years

dos: Name the handler on every shipment

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with a small embossed cog-and-anchor seal — the Hanseatic merchant mark — used on the consignment note, the wax seal, and the brass door plate.

colorPalette.name: Hanse Blue
colorPalette.meaning: The Baltic at dawn, the merchant-league livery.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and printed material
typography.secondary: Söhne for the secure client portal
typography.rationale: A high-contrast classical serif carries the merchant-house weight; the grotesk handles digital.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: The numbered loading dock — the universal physical unit of warehouse and cross-dock operations; 'Bay 7' is the kind of address a freight dispatcher actually uses. Strongest of Agent A's three for minimal: 'Hub' is good but generic, 'Long Haul' is fine but US-only register. Bay 7 has the specificity of a real address — it reads as a working warehouse, not a brand.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal 3PL serves DTC brands and small importers who don't need a national network — they need one warehouse that picks accurately and ships same-day. The opening is for a brand that names its dock.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: ShipBob (shipbob.com) holds the DTC-3PL peer. Shippo (goshippo.com) is the multi-carrier rate peer. Easyship (easyship.com) sits in the cross-border tier. ShipMonk (shipmonk.com) does the volume DTC slot. We sit smaller, single-dock.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A single-dock 3PL. Same-day pick. One named contact.

targetAudience.primary: DTC operations leads at 10-100 person brands shipping 50-5000 orders/day. They want one warehouse, one carrier mix, and one person who answers the phone.
behaviors: Books the warehouse tour before signing
Will switch 3PLs over a missed cutoff

dos: Publish the cutoff time on the home page
Confirm orders by SKU and dock

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. BAY 7 in a single-weight grotesk, with the 7 set as the dispatch numeral on a loading-bay sign. The numeral alone is the favicon.

typography.secondary: Neue Haas Grotesk Mono for tracking numbers
typography.rationale: One face. The mono carries the SKU and tracking; the regular carries the brand.

Corporate.tagline: Air-freight integration from the founding hub city.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Memphis, Tennessee — chosen by Fred Smith in 1973 as the FedEx superhub because of its central US location, mild weather, and underused airport; now the world's second-busiest cargo airport. Strongest of Agent A's three for corporate: 'Hapag Forwarding Group' has German maritime weight but reads less broadly to procurement; 'Lloyd's Register Freight' has trademark risk that Agent A flagged. Memphis Hub is the actual hub of global air-freight, broadly recognisable, no trademark exposure.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate air-freight integration in 2025+ is dominated by FedEx, UPS, DHL, and a handful of regional players. The opening is for a mid-tier integrator with hub discipline serving e-commerce, pharma cold-chain, and aerospace AOG.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: FedEx (fedex.com) holds the founding peer. UPS (ups.com) sits at the same tier. DHL Express (dhl.com) is the international peer. Atlas Air (atlasair.com) does the wide-body cargo middle. We sit smaller, mid-market.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A mid-tier air-freight integrator built on the original hub model.

targetAudience.primary: Supply-chain directors at e-commerce, pharma, and aerospace companies. They contract by lane and by time-definite product, and they care about on-time-delivery KPIs more than rate.

dos: Lead with on-time-delivery and lane capacity
Speak the language of supply-chain procurement

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left — three radiating lines from a single point, suggesting the hub-and-spoke network. Reads cleanly on aircraft livery, uniforms, and procurement decks.

colorPalette.name: Tarmac Navy
colorPalette.meaning: Night ramp, the cargo aircraft livery.

typography.primary: Inter for digital and procurement decks
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed scorecards and SLAs
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean; the serif handles printed quarterly business reviews.

Creative.tagline: The document that makes cargo real.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The cargo manifest — the master list of everything on board a ship or aircraft, required by customs authorities worldwide; the single document that summons a load into existence. Strongest of Agent A's three for creative: 'Last Mile Studio' is good but the phrase is overused in logistics; 'Bonded Warehouse Co' is specific but niche. Manifest has a double meaning (the document; the verb 'to make real') that gives the brand creative depth, and it's the one piece of paperwork every freight nerd recognises.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative freight-tech brands in 2025+ are a small but growing category — Project44, Flexport, and Loadsmart all do parts of the visibility/orchestration story. The opening is for a creative D2C/DTC freight brand that treats every shipment like a small editorial moment.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Project44 (project44.com) holds the visibility-platform peer. Convoy's collapse left a brand gap. Loadsmart (loadsmart.com) sits in the modern brokerage middle. Sennder (sennder.com) is the European peer. We sit warmer, more design-led.
Creative.positioningStatement: A freight-tech brand for shippers who want every load to tell its own story.

targetAudience.primary: Operations and brand leads at DTC and specialty-product brands. They care about the unboxing as much as the delivery, and they want the freight provider to participate in the brand.
behaviors: Wants the carrier branded on the LTL slip
Will pay a premium for the right paperwork design

dos: Design the bill of lading like a magazine spread
Publish the manifest as a weekly newsletter
Name every lane after a place

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a chunky display serif. The S of MANIFEST is set with a small ship-prow flourish. A standalone prow icon for stickers, social, and the LTL slip stamp.

typography.primary: GT Sectra Display for the wordmark and newsletter
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for waybill data
typography.rationale: The serif reads as printed document; the mono carries the cargo data.
